jd_requirements: Develop and tune controllers (PID, MPC, optimal/robust control) for dynamic nonlinear systems
Build and validate physical models for simulation, HIL testing, and autonomy
Train and deploy ML models for perception, planning, or adaptive control (supervised or RL)
Integrate algorithms with firmware and cloud teams, real-time safety and stability
Profile, optimize, and verify performance under latency, jitter, and compute constraints
System ID, RL (PPO/SAC) with safety shields
Large complex robotic systems with various sensors, multiple motors/robots

bullets.text: Developed a ROS2-based robotic system integrating a simulator and MPC controller, enabling precise obstacle avoidance and full trajectory completion with real-time state logging.

Integrated OptiTrack motion capture system with robotic platform, achieving <1 mm position accuracy and <10 ms latency, supporting real-time position feedback for closed-loop control in indoor environments.

Applied control system design and experimental validation to establish an OptiTrack-based real-time feedback pose control system, enabling sub-centimeter trajectory tracking and iterative controller refinement.
Led a 5-member cross-functional team to develop a hybrid flying-driving robot platform, achieving 100% integration of mobility and flight subsystems.
Developed embedded C firmware for STM32F407, enabling CAN-based motor control, BLE remote communication, and PID position control with +/-2 mm tracking error for an omnidirectional mobile robot.

Developed and tuned a dual-mode chassis control architecture with three PID loops managing translation and orientation, achieving <1.2 s error convergence and 40% improvement in directional stability.
Implemented a custom UART protocol with headers, footers, and float unpacking; leveraged DMA + interrupts for non-blocking 100 Hz updates of 6-DoF data, with <0.2% error rate.

edits.reason: Stronger action verb; 'used' is a banned starting word but also weak mid-sentence

bullets.text: Designed a modular PID-based navigation system on STM32 with inverse kinematics and yaw compensation, achieving omnidirectional motion and +/-0.1% global localization accuracy.
Independently developed an STM32-based control system using fuzzy PID algorithms for closed-loop stepper motor control, achieving +/-1 mm positioning accuracy.

Consolidated five functional boards into a single 4-layer PCB with KiCad, integrating control, power, and communication modules; reduced overall footprint by 40% and verified signal integrity via 100-MHz oscilloscope.

Designed a compact, low-power crane system with ESP32-based Wi-Fi remote control, enabling low-latency communication and autonomous coordination across multiple devices, achieving over 95% task repeatability.
Developed control programs for a six-axis CRP2 robotic arm using embedded C and ladder logic, enabling automated multi-axis motion for fuel rod testing.
Designed an STM32F103-based gateway to enable Modbus RTU communication between the PC and robotic controller, ensuring stable and real-time data exchange.
